2.4.1
All terms used in this guidance note have the same meaning as defined in the
above-mentioned legislation and regulatory instrument, unless the context
indicates otherwise.
A 'co-operative financial institution' is a co-operative that takes deposits and
chooses to identity itselt by use of the name Financial Co-operative, Financial
Services Co-operative, Credit Union or Savings and Credit Co-operative.
A 'prospective co-operative financial institution' is a collective whose members,
through a special resolution,
intend to apply to register as a
co-operative financial institution with the Prudential Authority under the
Co-operative Banks Act.
A 'registered co-operative financial institution' is a co-operative financial
institution that is registered with the Co-operative Banks Development Agency
(CBDA), in terms of Exemption Notice No. 620 of 2014 issued by the Registrar of
Banks (Registrar) in terms of the Banks Act 1990, (Act No. 94 of 1990), and is
applying to be registered with the Prudential Authority under the Co-operative
Banks Act.
Minimum requirements
Prudential Standard - TCFI-01 - details the requirements for registration of a
co-operative financial institution (CFl) with the Prudential Authority in terms of the
provisions of the Co-operative Banks Act. This guidance note is issued to assist
prospective and registered CFls to prepare the following documents, as
applicable, for submission to the Prudential Authority:
business plan;
savings policy; and
loans policy.
This guidance note sets out the minimum requirements against which the
Prudential Authority will assess the provisions of the aforementioned documents
of a prospective co-operative institution or a registered co-operative financial
institution as per Attachment 7: Governance and operational requirements for co-
operative financial institutions, of Prudential Standard - TCFI-01.
The proportional nature and size of the applicant will be taken into consideration
during the review of the documents.
The minimum requirements are captured as follows:
Business plan - Attachment 1;
2.4.2
Savings policy - Attachment 2; and
2.4.3
Loans policy - Attachment 3.

3.2
The business plan, savings and loans policies will be reviewed against the
requirements set out herein. Prospective co-operative financial institutions and
registered co-operative institutions are strongly encouraged to align their savings
and loans policies with these requirements and to ensure that their business
plans contain the minimum requirements set out herein.
Contact
A prospective or registered co-operative financial institution may contact the
Co-operative Banks Development Agency for assistance with their business plan,
savings policy or loans policy by e-mailing: CBDA@treasury.co.za.
The Prudential Authority may also be contacted by sending an e-mail to
SARB-PA@resbank.co.za with the subject line: CFI - Registration Assistance.
Dandy
Kuben Naidoo

sections.text: Attachment 2 — Savings Policy Attachment 2 - Savings Policy 1. Attachment 2 — Savings Policy Attachment 2 - Savings Policy 1. 1.1 1.2 2. 2.1 2.1.1 2.1.2 2.1.3 2.1.4 2.1.5 2.1.6 2.1.7 2.1.8 2.1.9 2.1.10 2.1.11 General ( The savings policy should be clearly detined and set torth in such a manner as to provide effective oversight by the directors and senior employees. The board of directors of every CFl has the responsibility to approve savings policies and to oversee implementation thereof. The savings policy should not be a static document, but should be reviewed periodically, at least once a year, and revised in light of changing circumstances surrounding the saving needs of the CFl members as well as changes that may occur within the CFl itself. Minimum provisions of a savings policy The following minimum requirements should be set out in the savings policy of a CFI: the objectives of the savings policy; the manner in which savings products are mobilised and marketed; persons responsible for policy review and the frequency of the review, which should not be less than once a year; the types of savings products offered by the CFl and the minimum requirements for accessing each savings product; mechanisms for proof of ownership of savings, notification methods and periods, e.g. savings books or quarterly savings statements; procedures for determining and adjusting interest rates and fees as well as treatment of interest capitalisation (which procedures must include the approval process for adjusting interest rates and fees); procedures for opening, closing and withdrawing from a savings account; development and authorisation of new savings products/services in compliance with the Co-operative Banks Act; handling charges for accounts considered to be inactive for a specified time period or due to the maintenance of minimum balances in the account (dormant accounts), including the responsibility and monitoring thereof; procedures for handling dormant accounts; reactivating dormant accounts, including the responsibility and monitoring thereof; 2.1.12 handling of charges for unpaid cheques, cancelled and/or disputed debit orders; Page 1 of 2 2.1.13 2.1.14 3.1 3.1.1 3.1.2 3.1.3 3.1.4 3.1.5 elimination of inactive accounts with marginal savings which have exceeded the specified time period; and the ability of the CFl to cancel savings accounts which have been handled in a dubious or irregular manner. Minimum provisions of a savings policy per product type The following minimum requirements should be set out in the savings policy for each type of savings product offered by the CFl: procedures for calculating interests on savings products as well as interest capitalisation where applicable; the calculation of interest rates and fees, where applicable; the criteria to invest in specific products, e.g. age, income source, etc.; the procedures for withdrawal of monies prior to maturity and penalties to be charged where applicable; and product terms, i.e. notice deposit, fixed deposit, etc. Page 2 of 2 Attachment 3 - Loans Policy 1. 1.1 1.2 2. 2.1 2.1.1 2.1.2 2.1.3 2.1.4 2.1.5 2.1.6 2.1.7 2.1.8 2.1.9 2.1.10 2.1.11 2.1.12 2.1.13 2.1.14 General The loan policy should be clearly defined and set forth in such a manner as to provide effective oversight by the board of directors and senior employees. The board of directors of every CFI has the responsibility to approve loans policies and to oversee implementation thereot. The loan policy should not be a static document, but must be reviewed periodically, at least once a year, and revised in light of changing circumstances surrounding the borrowing needs of the CFl members as well as changes that may occur within the CFl itself or changes in the legislation. Minimum provisions of a loans policy The following minimum requirements should be set out in the loan policy of a CFI: objective of the loan policy; persons responsible for policy review and the frequency of review, which should not be less than once a year; general fields of lending in which the CFI will engage and the kinds or types of loans within each general field; responsibility of the board of directors in reviewing, ratifying, or approving the loan policy; procedures for determining and adjusting interest rates and fees (which procedures must include the approval process for adjusting interest rates and fees); procedures to be followed when applying for credit; basis for determining an amount and period of a loan; procedures to be followed when evaluating and analysing loan applications; requirements to stipulate the purpose for which loan is requested; turnaround time for approving the loans; loan limits of each loan officer; loan limits, if any, of a credit committee; maintenance and review of complete and current credit files on each borrowing member; procedures for handling of conflict of interest regarding loans to employees, board members and related person(s); Page 1 of 3 2.1.15 2.1.16 2.1.17 2.1.18 2.1.19 2.1.20 2.1.21 2.1.22 2.1.23 2.1.24 3. 3.1 3.1.1 3.1.2 3.1.3 3.1.4 3.1.5 3.1.6 3.1.7 3.1.8 separation of duties with regards to the loan evaluation and the approval process; procedures for handling of loan concentration (large exposures in accordance with the prudential standard); procedures, which at a minimum, address the goals for portfolio mix and risk diversification and set out the CFl's plans for monitoring and taking appropriate corrective action, if deemed necessary, on any concentrations that may exist; defining delegated authority to approve loans with regards to unsecured risk and maximum loan sizes; loan rejection process; roles and responsibility of the credit committee, including procedures for the approval of the loans by the board; procedures for refinancing and/or restructuring of loans, where applicable; appropriate and adequate collection procedures including, but not limited to, actions to be taken against borrowers who fail to make timely payments; loan loss provision, if not a separate policy (delinquency loans must be provided for in accordance with the prudential standard); and compliance with the National Credit Act, 2005 (Act No. 34 of 2005), and other financial regulatory requirements. Minimum provisions of a loans policy per product type The following minimum requirements should be set out in the loans policy for each type of loan product offered by the CFl: statement regarding the waiting period to qualify for credit; period and manner in which loan repayments must be made; manner in which interest rate will be determined (i.e. fixed or variable); period and manner, including grace periods, on which interest on loans will be calculated; calculation of interest and fees; supporting documentation to be used; treatment of guarantees, where applicable; acceptance of security, the completion of documentation when security is granted, and the treatment thereof in the event of a default; Page 2 of 3 3.1.9 3.1.10 3.1.11 3.1.12 3.1.13 stipulation of maximum loan period; order in which loan repayments are allocated (tees, interest, principal amount etc.); determination of how arrear interest and charges will accrue in relation to outstanding loan balances upon default; manner in which communication with members will be handled, i.e. at inception, periodic statements, etc.; and provision for loan protection, including, but not limited to, credit life policies.
